newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power moves up sharply ahead of cold.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power moves up sharply ahead of cold.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) moved sharply higher Thursday in anticipation of significant power demand from much below normal temperatures Friday, sources said.
Forecasts called for Friday highs in north Texas to be near freezing, while temperatures in south Texas were expected to reach the high 30s degrees Fahrenheit.
Temperatures were expected to rebound through the weekend, however with some above-normal temperatures by the beginning of next week.

ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Friday delivery was discussed at $54.00-59.00 from $37.00-41.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Wednesday for Thursday delivery, the brokers and marketers said.
ERCOT non-firm peak power was talked at $47.00-52.00 from $33.00-35.00 per MWh on Wednesday, the sources said.
Spot natural gas for Friday delivery in Texas was also said to be expensive in the $4.60s per million British thermal units level.
Several sources said a Texas utility had planned to shut a nuclear unit over the weekend for maintenance, but decided to postpone the outage in light of the cold weather.

Texas Utilities said its nuclear plants were at full operation with no weekend outages expected. Houston Lighting and Power would not comment on the status of its generation plants or any plans for a weekend outage.
Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Friday were talked at $29.00-31.00 from talk at $24.50-28.50 per MWh on Wednesday.
February ERCOT peak power was said to have moved lower in line with a downturn in natural gas futures, with Thursday discussion at $31.50-33.50 from $33.00-36.00 on Wednesday.
